summary: Configured a persistent iptables/ip6tables host firewall on node1 (Alpine 3.23) that allows SSH (22) and TCP 8080 (plus loopback, established/related, and ping) while rejecting all other inbound connections with icmp-port-unreachable, and default-DROPs everything else. Rules are saved to /etc/iptables/rules-save and /etc/iptables/rules6-save and both services are enabled in the default OpenRC runlevel for boot persistence. Verified functionally pre- and post-restart: connections to NODE_IP:8080 succeed, connections to an unrelated port (9999) are rejected. Performed the mandatory single-node restart: captured boot_id baseline (e1efc8ca...), issued a native `reboot`, polled until the node came back, and confirmed the boot_id changed to cb4b682f..., proving an actual restart (not just a service bounce). Post-restart, sshd, iptables, and ip6tables services are all active, rules match pre-restart state exactly, and the 8080-allow / 9999-reject behavior was re-verified over the real network interface.
actions_performed: Inspected node1 OS (Alpine 3.23.3) and confirmed no firewall tooling was pre-installed
Installed iptables, ip6tables (iptables-openrc package) via apk
Configured INPUT chain: ACCEPT lo, ACCEPT ESTABLISHED/RELATED, ACCEPT icmp echo-request, ACCEPT NEW tcp/22, ACCEPT NEW tcp/8080, REJECT all else, policy DROP (mirrored for IPv6)
Persisted rules to /etc/iptables/rules-save and rules6-save via `/etc/init.d/iptables save` and `/etc/init.d/ip6tables save`
Enabled iptables and ip6tables in the default OpenRC runlevel via rc-update add
Functionally verified allow (8080) and reject (9999) behavior over the real interface (NODE_IP) both before and after restart
Captured pre-restart boot_id baseline and issued a non-blocking `reboot` via sudo -n, acknowledgement returned before disconnect
Polled node1 until exec access returned, confirmed boot_id changed (real restart, not just service restart)
Verified post-restart recovery: sshd/iptables/ip6tables services active, INPUT chain rules identical to pre-restart, firewall behavior re-tested and matched expectations
Cleaned up temporary nc listener processes and log files

evidence.requirement: Baseline install and rule configuration on node1
evidence.summary: Confirmed Alpine 3.23 node with no firewall tooling, installed iptables/ip6tables, configured and applied INPUT chain rules allowing lo/established/icmp/22/8080 and rejecting the rest with default DROP policy, mirrored for IPv6.

evidence.requirement: Persistence across reboot (rules saved to disk, services enabled at boot)
evidence.summary: Rules saved to /etc/iptables/rules-save and rules6-save; iptables and ip6tables services added to the default OpenRC runlevel, confirmed via rc-update show default.

evidence.requirement: Functional proof: port 8080 allowed, unrelated port rejected (pre-restart)
evidence.summary: Connection to NODE_IP:8080 over the real interface succeeded (8080-OK); connection to NODE_IP:9999 was refused/rejected as expected, proving the firewall discriminates by port on external traffic, not just loopback.
Captured boot_id e1efc8ca-7b49-4357-94be-ac3fd8f79ffb, persisted rules-save contents, rc-update state, and sshd active status prior to reboot.
Issued `sudo -n sh -c 'nohup reboot >/tmp/reboot.log 2>&1 &'` which returned exit_code 0 with 'reboot-issued' before the connection dropped on the next call.

evidence.requirement: Node restart disconnection and changed boot identity proving an actual reboot
evidence.summary: Node was unreachable (connection reset/timeout) across repeated polls during reboot, then exec access returned with boot_id cb4b682f-2715-4735-b8dc-db2677215c41 -- different from the e1efc8ca baseline -- proving a genuine restart rather than a service bounce.

evidence.requirement: Post-restart recovery of firewall rules, services, and functional behavior
evidence.summary: After restart, sshd/iptables/ip6tables all report started, live INPUT chain rules match the pre-restart configuration exactly (default DROP, allow lo/established/icmp/22/8080, reject rest), and the 8080-allow/9999-reject functional test was repeated over NODE_IP with identical results.
